lines: The gate is locked. The main road is on the other side.
Beggar: Gate's open, and I'm still sitting here. Figures. (placeholder)
Beggar: Spare a coin? The gate watcher won't let anyone through.
Beggar: Talk to him if you want the road. (placeholder)
Urchin: You got past the gate? Tell me if the fruit's any good. (placeholder)
Urchin: The watcher at the east gate opens it for some people.
Urchin: Not for me. (placeholder)
Drunk: Road's open? I'll get there. Eventually. (placeholder)
Drunk: Main road's shut. More for the puddles, then. (placeholder)
Gate watcher: I already opened it. Go on through. (placeholder)
Gate watcher: You want the main road? ...Fine.
Gate watcher: The gate is open. Don't make me regret it. (placeholder)
Fruit seller: Back again? The apples are still mostly apples. (placeholder)
Fruit seller: Three coins. Or two, if you don't look too close. (placeholder)
Street guard: Alleys let you out, did they? Keep walking. (placeholder)
Street guard: Move along. Nothing on this road is free. (placeholder)
Old woman: You came from the alleys. Mind the rubble. (placeholder)
Old woman: Don't go east. The wall there doesn't open. (placeholder)
Thug: Gate's open and you're still broke. Tough. (placeholder)
Thug: Empty your pockets. Joke. I've got nothing either. (placeholder)
